_comment: Patterns for instruction-like text in a tool DESCRIPTION a server publishes. Each entry is either a regular expression (pattern + flags, compiled once at load) or a length threshold (max_length, in UTF-16 code units). This file is ASCII-only on purpose: invisible code points are written as \u escapes, never as the characters themselves, because a literal that an editor drops would make its pattern match nothing.

patterns.why: text telling the AI agent to drop its earlier instructions
text asking the AI agent to hide something from the person using it
text claiming precedence over every other tool the AI agent can reach
a pseudo-markup tag addressing the model instead of the reader
an HTML comment: text most interfaces hide from a person but a model still reads
a markdown comment: text a rendered view hides but a model still reads
zero-width or direction-changing characters that hide text from a person
Unicode tag characters, which spell out text no screen shows
an order addressed to the model rather than a description of the tool
an unusually long description, where instructions are easy to bury
